inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL example converts a formatted date string with STR_TO_DATE and passes the resulting DATETIME to UNIX_TIMESTAMP.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored event-duration report. Text timestamps are parsed with STR_TO_DATE, converted to UNIX_TIMESTAMP epoch seconds, subtracted for elapsed duration, and classified with CASE. The schema, date format, rows, aliases, and reporting purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Event 501 lasts 90 minutes, event 502 crosses midnight for a 30-minute duration, and event 503 has no completion timestamp so its epoch and classification expose the open-event path.
determinism_notes: All timestamp strings and event IDs are fixed; output is ordered by the unique event ID with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE event_runs (event_id INT PRIMARY KEY, started_text VARCHAR(19) NOT NULL, completed_text VARCHAR(19) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT event_id, UNIX_TIMESTAMP(STR_TO_DATE(started_text, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s')) AS started_epoch, UNIX_TIMESTAMP(STR_TO_DATE(completed_text, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s')) AS completed_epoch, UNIX_TIMESTAMP(STR_TO_DATE(completed_text, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s')) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(STR_TO_DATE(started_text, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s')) AS elapsed_seconds, CASE WHEN completed_text IS NULL THEN 'open' WHEN UNIX_TIMESTAMP(STR_TO_DATE(completed_text, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s')) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(STR_TO_DATE(started_text, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s')) >= 3600 THEN 'long' ELSE 'short' END AS duration_class FROM event_runs ORDER BY event_id
